# University of the Andes (Colombia) Summary
Founded in 1948 by Mario Laserna Pinzón and intellectuals from Colombia's elite, the University of the Andes (Uniandes) was Colombia’s first nonsectarian and politically independent university, established to provide skilled professionals to support the country’s industrial growth. Modeled after American universities, it began academic activities in 1949 with 80 students, emphasizing a liberal and technical education to foster leaders equipped with international knowledge. Despite political turmoil in the 1950s, Uniandes maintained political neutrality and developed programs such as the "three/two" transfer with U.S. institutions, and actively recruited foreign faculty to enhance its academic stature.
Legally established as a nonprofit in 1948 and granted university status in 1964, Uniandes is governed by a Board of Trustees, Board of Directors, and Academic Council, comprising various administrative and faculty bodies. With 14 academic units including faculties and interdisciplinary centers, the university supports over 1,500 non-faculty staff. Its mission emphasizes pluralism, diversity, academic excellence, and social responsibility. The main campus in Bogotá features a blend of restored historic and modern facilities, with substantial classrooms, laboratories, and libraries. Uniandes engages globally through exchange programs with over 119 universities. Its mascot is a goat named Seneca, symbolizing student tradition. Distinguished alumni include former Colombian presidents, ministers, esteemed artists, and scientists.
